kjv: The LORD our God [is] one LORD
mine: Yahweh our God, Yahweh is one
note: The verbless Hebrew YHWH 'eloheinu YHWH 'echad can be parsed several ways: "Yahweh our God, Yahweh is one" (unity) or "Yahweh is our God, Yahweh alone" (exclusive loyalty, fitting the following call to undivided love); the KJV takes the oneness reading. Context: Yahweh our God, Yahweh is one (parsing left open) (medium confidence). A verbless clause. 'Echad normally means 'one' ('alone' is usually levad), and LXX kyrios heis estin and Mark 12:29-32 read 'one'. Leaving the first half verbless, as ESV, NIV and CSB do, keeps open both 'Yahweh our God is one Yahweh' and 'Yahweh is our God, Yahweh is one/alone'; 6:5 and 6:14-15 stress exclusive loyalty. Other possible meanings: (1) 'Yahweh is our God, Yahweh alone' — NRSV/NRSVue, NJPS, many commentators ('echad as 'only', cf. 1 Chr 29:1; Zech 14:9); (2) 'Yahweh our God is one Yahweh' — LXX, Mark 12:29, KJV, ESV/NIV notes; (3) 'Yahweh is our God; Yahweh is one', two clauses stressing his unity — NASB, NET.

kjv: Ye shall not tempt the LORD your God
mine: You shall not put Yahweh your God to the test
note: Hebrew nissah means to test or try someone (cf. massah, "testing"); "tempt" now suggests enticing to sin.
